\section{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov: Introduction}
Bobkov's functional measures the expected Euclidean length of a Gaussian profile together with the discrete gradient. The cube inequality bounds the profile of the mean, and the functional is monotone in the Boolean noise correlation.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov: Results}

\begin{definition}[Expected profile-gradient length]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p021-b001}
For a real function $f$ on the uniform Boolean cube $\{0,1\}^n$, write $D_i f(x)=(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})-f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))/2$ and $B(f)=\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_i(D_i f)^2}$, where $\overline I$ is the Gaussian profile extended by zero outside $(0,1)$. The Bobkov functional assigns the value $B(f)$ to $f$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
Let $a,b\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $a+b\in[0,1]$ and $a-b\in[0,1]$. Then the closed Gaussian
profile satisfies
\[
U(a)\le \frac{\sqrt{U(a+b)^2+b^2}+\sqrt{U(a-b)^2+b^2}}{2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Mean of a bounded Boolean function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.expect_mem_unitInterval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\le f(x)\le1$ for every
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Then its uniform expectation satisfies $0\le\E[f]\le1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bobkov functional in dimension zero]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional_zero_dim}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\difficulty{1}
For every real-valued function $f$ on the zero-dimensional Boolean cube, $B(f)=\overline
I(\mathbb E f)$, where $\overline I$ is the closed Gaussian profile and the expectation
is under the uniform measure on that cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Profile inequality for restricted means]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.profile_mean_restrictions_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_two_point, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.expect_diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.expect_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ take values in $[0,1]$. For
$b\in\{0,1\}$, let $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$ and let $d(x)=\tfrac12(f_0(x)-f_1(x))$. If $U$ is the
Gaussian profile that equals $\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and $0$ otherwise, then
\[
U(\mathbb E f)\le\frac{\sqrt{U(\mathbb E f_0)^2+(\mathbb E d)^2}+\sqrt{U(\mathbb E
f_1)^2+(\mathbb E d)^2}}{2},
\]
where all expectations are uniform on the corresponding Boolean cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity after adding a squared coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_profile_sq_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a dimension, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$\{0,1\}^n$, and let $d\in\mathbb R$. If the closed Gaussian profile at the expectation
of $f$ is at most the Bobkov functional of $f$, then $\sqrt{\overline
I(\E[f])^2+d^2}\le\sqrt{B(f)^2+d^2}$, where $\overline I$ denotes the closed Gaussian
profile and $B(f)$ the Bobkov functional.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length identity under coordinate restriction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.restricted_length_identity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sum_sq_derivative_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.derivative}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ and
$x\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $f_b$ be the restriction of $f$ to last coordinate $b$, let $D_i$
denote the coordinate half-difference, and let $U$ be the Gaussian profile equal to
$\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and zero otherwise. Then the Euclidean length formed
from $U(f_b(x))$, the derivatives $D_i f_b(x)$ for $i<n$, and the half-difference
$(f_0(x)-f_1(x))/2$ equals the Euclidean length formed from $U(f(x,b))$ and all
derivatives $D_i f(x,b)$ for $i<n+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bound for a restricted contribution]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.restriction_contribution_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.restricted_length_identity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_expect_sq_add_sq_le_expect_sqrt, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.sqrt_profile_sq_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, and choose
$b\in\{0,1\}$. Let $f_b$ be the restriction to last coordinate $b$, let
$d(x)=(f(x,0)-f(x,1))/2$, and let $U$ be the Gaussian profile equal to
$\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$ and zero otherwise. If $U(\mathbb E f_b)\le B(f_b)$,
where expectation is uniform on the cube and $B(g)=\mathbb E_x\sqrt{U(g(x))^2+\sum_i(D_i
g(x))^2}$, then $\sqrt{U(\mathbb E f_b)^2+(\mathbb E d)^2}\le\mathbb
E_x\sqrt{U(f(x,b))^2+\sum_{i<n+1}(D_i f(x,b))^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bobkov inequality on the Boolean cube]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_inequality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional_zero_dim, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.profile_mean_restrictions_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.restriction_contribution_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_succ_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.expect}

\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$. Then the closed Gaussian profile
evaluated at the uniform expectation of $f$ is at most its Bobkov functional: $\overline
I(\mathbb E f)\le B(f)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Noise contraction of the Bobkov functional]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional_noise_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.extendedFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.BobkovInterpolation.extendedFunctional_noise_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkov_two_point, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.closedGaussianProfile_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.continuousOn_closedGaussianProfile, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$, and let $0\le\rho\le1$. Then the
Bobkov functional of the Boolean noise operator applied to $f$ satisfies $B(T_\rho f)\le
B(f)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the Bobkov functional under noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional_noise_monotone}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.bobkovFunctional_noise_le, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_compose, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$. The map $\rho\mapsto B(T_\rho f)$
is nondecreasing on $[0,1]$; that is, whenever $0\le\rho_1\le\rho_2\le1$, one has
$B(T_{\rho_1}f)\le B(T_{\rho_2}f)$.
\end{theorem}
